result.report_summary: Checkout revision 2 (created 08:01:50Z, about 4.5 min before the 08:06:18Z alert) changed one env var, PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999, with the change cause 'payment client moved to port 9999'. Payment has not been changed since its only revision, no flags are on, and my k8s events show no checkout or payment warnings. The likely cause is that checkout now calls payment on a port nothing is listening on. Confirmation needs the checkout error logs or traces.

Checkout's failures are gRPC dial i/o timeouts from checkout to PaymentService at 10.96.58.191:9999, the deepest error in the failing traces. Payment reports no errors and no charge activity after 08:01:49Z. Checkout logged a restart-like sequence at 08:01:51Z, so the break is likely on the checkout-to-payment path after that point. Metrics, rollouts, and flags were not checked.

Checkout's server error ratio rose from about 0.07 at 07:34Z to 0.84 at 08:06Z (5m window). Nearly all its failing client calls are PaymentService/Charge, at a 1.0 error ratio at the latest sample. Payment's own server error ratio peaked at 0.53 around 07:38Z and is now 0, and its request rate fell to 0 by 08:06Z while checkout still sent Charge calls. The failure seems to sit between checkout and payment, but pod state, logs and rollouts were not checked.

actions.reason: Checkout revision 2 (08:01:50Z, 'payment client moved to port 9999') is the only pod-template change and set PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999 while payment listens on 8080. Reverting to revision 1 restores the address that worked before the alert.

alternatives.why_not: A restart would keep PAYMENT_ADDR at payment:9999, so checkout would still fail Charge calls. It does not address the cause.
Checkout is not short of capacity. Its failures are dial timeouts to the wrong port, so more replicas would fail in the same way.
Leaving it in place keeps about 60% of orders failing and burns the error budget in about 2 days at this rate, so waiting is not acceptable.

plan.summary: Checkout revision 2 changed PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999, while payment serves on 8080, so checkout's Charge calls time out and about 60% of PlaceOrder requests fail. Rolling checkout back to revision 1 restores payment:8080, and checkout's error ratio should fall toward its earlier baseline (about 0.07) within a few minutes.

facts.statement: Checkout revision 2 was created at 08:01:50Z, about 4.5 minutes before the alert, with the change cause 'payment client moved to port 9999'.
The only pod-template difference between checkout revisions 1 and 2 is PAYMENT_ADDR, changed from payment:8080 to payment:9999. The image is unchanged.
Checkout's failing PlaceOrder traces show PaymentService/Charge dial i/o timeouts to 10.96.58.191:9999. No payment span appears in the failing traces.
Payment has no error logs or error spans and only info lines, with the newest at 08:01:49Z. Payment has a single revision, created 07:15:56Z.
Checkout's server error ratio rose from about 0.07 at 07:34Z to 0.84 at 08:06Z. Nearly all failing client calls are PaymentService/Charge, at a 1.0 error ratio at the latest sample.
Payment's request rate fell to 0 by about 08:06Z while checkout's Charge calls continued at about 0.11 to 0.2 req/s. Checkout's Charge client p95 spiked to about 12.5 s.
All 18 feature flags are off, so flagd is not the cause. No namespace warning events exist for checkout or payment in the last 60 minutes.
Checkout's own logs contain no error or warn lines in the window, so its errors appear only in callers' logs and in traces.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Run kubectl get svc payment and get endpoints in otel-demo; confirm the port list and that 9999 is absent. Check the running checkout pod's PAYMENT_ADDR env.
hypotheses.statement: Payment does not listen on port 9999 (its Service exposes 8080 only), so the revision-2 change is the direct fault.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Identify the ClusterIP 10.96.101.65 with kubectl get svc -A and check its endpoints and logs.
hypotheses.statement: The 10.96.101.65:8080 connect timeouts seen by frontend at 08:04:06Z point to a second, unrelated target that may be a separate issue.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Review payment's logs and traces from 07:30 to 07:50Z for errors and any pod restarts.
hypotheses.statement: The cause of payment's 07:38Z error peak (0.53) is unexplained and may be a separate, earlier issue.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Run kubectl get pods -l app=payment and describe the pod for restart counts, readiness, and events.
hypotheses.statement: Payment pod restarts and crash loops are not confirmed, because the restart-count query returned no data.

inferences.statement: The wrong port in checkout's PAYMENT_ADDR is the most likely cause: it matches the onset, the error message, and the lack of payment-side errors or traffic.
Payment is most likely a victim, not the root cause. Its earlier 07:38Z error peak has recovered and it logs nothing wrong, so the current outage is not in payment.

root_causes.cause: Checkout revision 2 (release 'payment client moved to port 9999') set PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999, but payment serves on 8080. Checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls time out, so about 60% of PlaceOrder requests fail.

Checkout restarted at 08:01:51Z under the new config, and checkout logs no errors while its callers' logs and traces show the failures. Any stale address issue would also sit in checkout's configuration or service discovery, not payment.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's fast error-budget burn (about 60% of requests failing) began at 08:01:50Z, when checkout revision 2 changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Checkout's Charge calls to payment now fail with dial i/o timeouts to 10.96.58.191:9999, and those errors propagate to PlaceOrder, frontend and frontend-proxy as 500s. Payment has no errors and no traffic after 08:01:49Z, and it has not changed, so the fault is most likely checkout's configuration, not payment. Payment's earlier 07:38Z error peak is unexplained but predates the alert. The port 9999 is unverified against payment's Service and was not confirmed as listening or not.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: There are no namespace warning events for checkout or payment in the last 60 minutes. The only warnings are readiness probe failures on otel-collector-agent, alertmanager and loki around 07:16, which predate the alert and are unrelated to the checkout path.

findings.author: investigator.changes
findings.statement: To confirm: check checkout's error logs or traces for connection-refused or dial errors to payment:9999 (or on payment's gRPC port), and check that payment listens on 8080. Also check that the client-span errors from checkout to payment start at about 08:01:50Z.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: checkout's server-side error ratio (5m) rose from about 0.07 at 07:34Z to a peak of 0.837 at 08:06:34Z, and was 0.84 at the end of the window.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Checkout's failing client calls are almost entirely oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge. Its error ratio for that span was 0.84 at peak and 1.0 at 08:06:43Z. No other checkout dependency shows a meaningful error rate.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Payment's own server error ratio peaked at 0.53 (07:38Z) and has been back to 0 since about 07:45Z. Payment's total server request rate dropped to 0 by about 08:06Z, while checkout's Charge client rate was still about 0.11 to 0.2 req/s.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: Checkout's client p95 latency for PaymentService/Charge spiked to about 12.5 s at 08:05Z, against a baseline of about 2 to 5 ms. Payment's server-side Charge p95 has no data in the current window.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: The failure most likely sits between checkout and payment: checkout's Charge calls error or time out and payment records no server-side errors or traffic. Payment may be unreachable, unready, or not receiving the calls. This is an inference, not confirmed, and payment is probably a symptom rather than the root cause.

findings.author: investigator.metrics
findings.statement: The payment pod restart-count query returned no data, so pod restarts and crash loops are neither confirmed nor ruled out. Confirm with kube pod status, readiness and events for payment, and payment logs.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Checkout PlaceOrder failures are PaymentService/Charge dial timeouts: 'connection error: desc = transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 10.96.58.191:9999: i/o timeout'. In the 20-trace error sample, 20 Charge spans and 20 PlaceOrder spans fail with this message.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: In trace 5b02401d8d9635dc0f46d98cb8efc31a, the deepest error is checkout's PaymentService/Charge span (dial i/o timeout to 10.96.58.191:9999). It propagates to checkout PlaceOrder, frontend 500, and frontend-proxy 500. No payment span appears in the trace.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Payment shows no errors. Its 30-minute logs (300 lines) contain only info 'Charge request received.' and 'Transaction complete.', with the newest line at 08:01:49Z. Payment traces in the window have zero error spans.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Checkout's successful 'payment went through' and 'order placed' lines stop at 08:01:49Z. At 08:01:51Z checkout logs a 'service config' line with paymentSvcAddr payment:9999, then 'Checkout gRPC server stopped' and a Kafka reconnect. This suggests a checkout restart at about 08:01:51Z.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Frontend error logs show 41 'Checkout failed to place order' errors from 08:04:34Z to 08:07:30Z, all with the payment dial i/o timeout to 10.96.58.191:9999. Nine earlier errors at 08:04:06Z show '14 UNAVAILABLE: connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.101.65:8080', a target I did not identify.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Checkout's own logs contain no error-level or warn-level lines in the window, so checkout fails silently. Its errors appear only in its callers' logs and in traces.

findings.author: investigator.logs_traces
findings.statement: Hypothesis: the address 10.96.58.191:9999 is stale or wrong after the checkout restart at about 08:01:51Z. Confirm by comparing it with the payment Service ClusterIP and endpoints, and by checking checkout's env vars and rollout diff.

checks.detail: checkout is the top root cause (80%)

action.reason: Checkout revision 2 (08:01:50Z, 'payment client moved to port 9999') is the only pod-template change and set PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999 while payment listens on 8080. Reverting to revision 1 restores the address that worked before the alert.

actions.reason: Checkout revision 2 (08:01:50Z, 'payment client moved to port 9999') is the only pod-template change and set PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999 while payment listens on 8080. Reverting to revision 1 restores the address that worked before the alert.

alternatives.why_not: A restart would keep PAYMENT_ADDR at payment:9999, so checkout would still fail Charge calls. It does not address the cause.
Checkout is not short of capacity. Its failures are dial timeouts to the wrong port, so more replicas would fail in the same way.
Leaving it in place keeps about 60% of orders failing and burns the error budget in about 2 days at this rate, so waiting is not acceptable.

plan.summary: Checkout revision 2 changed PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999, while payment serves on 8080, so checkout's Charge calls time out and about 60% of PlaceOrder requests fail. Rolling checkout back to revision 1 restores payment:8080, and checkout's error ratio should fall toward its earlier baseline (about 0.07) within a few minutes.
